reasoning: Combined the two trivia-label rules into one replacement that covers both punctuated and flattened prompts. Kept the title, nickname, and proverb completion guidance, plus the three distinct clue-format rules from the second patch. Support counts reflect how many of the two source patches support each edit; no edits target protected content.

edits.target: For fragmentary quotes or titles, prefer a direct completion supported by context over a merely related result.
edits.content: For fragmentary quotes, titles, nicknames, or familiar sayings and proverbs, infer the omitted word or phrase that completes the clue rather than echoing the supplied text. Return only the identifying portion requested: do not repeat title wording already supplied by the clue or append a generic class word when it is implicit, unless the full name is requested or needed to distinguish the answer.

edits.target: In trivia-style passages, headings or labels before a colon may be categories rather than answers; solve the clue itself.
edits.content: In trivia-style lists, clue text, category labels, and answer-length markers may run together with or without punctuation. A heading or label before a colon—or a trailing label or parenthetical number—may be metadata for the following clue, including when it appears immediately after the previous clue. Do not assign such metadata to the preceding clue or return it as the answer; solve the clue itself using its meaning and corroborating context.

When a prompt consists only of a list of character names or roles, use context to identify their shared work or program if that is the implied target. Return the work or program, not the performers, unless the prompt asks for the cast.

For compact definition or wordplay clues that give two linked readings, solve the whole clue for the conventional term satisfying both; do not merely restate one reading. Preserve an article when it is part of the expected expression.

Honor the measurement or attribute explicitly requested: for example, “smallest in size” asks about physical dimensions, not denomination or value. Do not substitute a related property for the stated one; use evidence about the requested property.
